html:
SMTO-SKL-0107 — That Microsoft account type isn't allowed for this connection

GUID: d80e1f78-e503-537e-84f3-bd0ecb4e6be2
Slug: microsoft365-tenant-mismatch
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • You signed in with a Microsoft account this connection doesn't accept, such as a personal account where only work or school accounts are allowed. The account was not connected.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the Agent to connect your Microsoft 365 account again. Each attempt needs a fresh sign-in link.
  2. On Microsoft's account picker, choose your work or school account, or your personal account, whichever this connection is set up for. Microsoft lists both kinds, and only the kind this connection allows will work.
  3. If you're not sure which kind is allowed, ask the person who manages SMTO which Microsoft account the connection was set up for. Only they can see which organization the connection accepts.

What success looks like

  • The browser page says your account is connected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change the connection to accept every Microsoft account just to get past this; that lets accounts from other organizations sign in.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • verify_identity found the signed ID token's tenant (tid) conflicts with the Microsoft OAuth App's tenant setting (consumers vs organizations, or a specific tenant ID/domain whose issuer does not match).

What this means

  • Verified token tenant conflicts with the configured consumer, organization or exact tenant restriction. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Verified token tenant conflicts with the configured consumer, organization or exact tenant restriction.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare verified tenant identity with the app's deliberate tenant restriction.

How to fix it

  • Sign in with an account from the tenant configured on the Microsoft OAuth App (tenant field). If a different tenant is intended, change the app registration's supported account types in Entra and the tenant field in Parameter Store deliberately; SMTO never broadens it to common automatically.
  • Use an account accepted by the app registration tenant; do not broaden the configured tenant automatically.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account matches the registered app restriction without silently broadening it.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
